headline: A plus, plus, plus
dek: The day after asking Congress to stand up for him, the President gives his Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, an “A” PLUS, PLUS, PLUS, and calls Thomas Massie, whom he describes as a defeated former congressman, a total loser.

original.speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Pete Hegseth gets an “A” PLUS, PLUS, PLUS for his defense against a disgruntled, angry, defeated, former Congressman, Thomas Massie, a TOTAL LOSER!
President DJT
original.key: Pete Hegseth gets an “A” PLUS, PLUS, PLUS for his defense against a disgruntled, angry, defeated, former Congressman, Thomas Massie, a TOTAL LOSER!
original.context: Posted on the morning of 10 November 2026, the day after “Congress, stand up for Pete!!!” (see “Praised, not impeached”). Thomas Massie is a Republican congressman from Kentucky; the President calls him defeated and former.

verification.note: Copied by the editor from truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump on 10 November 2026 (shown as 11/10/26, 5:33 AM Pacific).

en: Secretary Hegseth has defended his record well, and I commend him for it.
I respect Representative Thomas Massie’s right to disagree, but I stand fully behind the Secretary, and I trust that Congress will too.
fr: Le secrétaire Hegseth a bien défendu son bilan, et je l’en félicite.
Je respecte le droit du représentant Thomas Massie d’être en désaccord, mais je soutiens pleinement le secrétaire, et j’ai confiance que le Congrès en fera autant.
presidential.key: Secretary Hegseth has defended his record well, and I commend him for it.

valaisan.hook: Un A plus, plus, plus ! *Chez nous, c’est un 6. Et c’est déjà beaucoup.*
valaisan.hookEn: An A plus, plus, plus! *Round here it’s a 6. And that’s already a lot.*
valaisan.short: Chez nous, à l’école, il n’y a pas de A : la meilleure note, c’est 6. *Alors disons 6. Plus, plus, plus.*
valaisan.shortEn: Swiss schools don’t give A’s: the top grade is 6. *So let’s say 6. Plus, plus, plus.*
text: Adieu ! Pete Hegseth, je lui mets un A plus, plus, plus pour sa défense contre ce Massie, un aigri, un fâché, un perdant total.
Mais chez nous, à l’école, il n’y a pas de A : la meilleure note, c’est 6. Alors disons 6 plus, plus, plus. Et le Massie, qu’il aille réfléchir en suivant un bisse. C’est long, et ça calme.
en: Adieu! Pete Hegseth gets an A plus, plus, plus from me for his defence against that Massie, a sourpuss, an angry man, a total loser.

But round here, at school, there are no A’s: the top grade is 6. So let’s say 6 plus, plus, plus. As for Massie, he can go and think it over walking along a bisse. It takes a while, and it calms you down.
notes: Swiss school grades go from 1 to 6, and 6 is the best. The bisses are the old irrigation channels of Valais, with long walking paths beside them.

genevois.hook: Un A plus, plus, plus ! *Ici, on dit triple A. Et on le range au coffre.*
genevois.hookEn: An A plus, plus, plus! *Here we say triple A. And we lock it in the vault.*
genevois.short: À Genève, un A plus, plus, plus, on appelle ça un triple A. On le range au coffre, sans en parler. *Moi, j’en parle.*
genevois.shortEn: In Geneva, an A plus plus plus is a triple A. You lock it in the vault and say nothing. *I don’t.*
text: Pete Hegseth, je lui mets un A plus, plus, plus pour sa défense contre ce Thomas Massie, aigri, fâché, et, je le dis, un perdant total.
Remarquez, à Genève, un A plus, plus, plus, on appelle ça un triple A, et on le range au coffre, au fond de la banque, sans en parler à personne. Moi, j’en parle. C’est toute la différence.
en: Pete Hegseth gets an A plus, plus, plus from me for his defence against that Thomas Massie, bitter, angry and, I’ll say it, a total loser.
Mind you, in Geneva an A plus, plus, plus is called a triple A, and you put it in the vault, at the back of the bank, without telling anyone. Me, I tell everyone. That’s the difference.
notes: Switzerland holds the top “AAA” credit rating, and Geneva is one of the capitals of discreet private banking.

sud.hookEn: 25 out of 20! *Yes, that exists. Down here.*
sud.short: Chez nous, la note maximale, c’est 20. Moi, je lui mets 25 sur 20. *Oui, ça existe. Ici.*
sud.shortEn: In France the top mark is 20 out of 20. I give him 25. *Yes, that exists. Down here.*
text: Pete Hegseth, je lui mets A plus, plus, plus, pour sa défense contre ce Massie, un aigri, un énervé, un perdant total, fan de chichoune !
Et encore, je suis modeste : moi, je lui mets 25 sur 20. Oui, ça existe, ici. Et le Massie, zéro pointé, et je suis gentil, parce qu’à Marseille, on n’exagère jamais.
en: Pete Hegseth gets an A plus, plus, plus from me for his defence against that Massie, a sourpuss, a hothead, a total loser, good grief!
And I’m being modest: I give him 25 out of 20. Yes, that exists, down here. And Massie gets a big fat zero, and that’s me being kind, because in Marseille we never exaggerate.
notes: French schools mark out of 20, and a 20 is very rare. “Fan de chichoune!” is a Marseille exclamation of surprise.

chti.hook: Un A plus, plus, plus ! *Chez nous, c’est des moules-frites à volonté.*
chti.hookEn: An A plus, plus, plus! *Up north, that’s all-you-can-eat mussels and fries.*
chti.short: Dans le Nord, la meilleure note, c’est une place à la braderie avec une montagne de moules-frites. *Massie, toi, tu fais la vaisselle.*
chti.shortEn: Up north, the top grade is a seat at the Lille braderie with a mountain of mussels and fries. *Massie does the dishes.*
text: Pete Hegseth, il mérite un A plus, plus, plus, pour sa défense contre ce Massie, un aigri, un grincheux, un perdant total.

Dans le Nord, la meilleure récompense, c’est pas une note : c’est une place à la table de la braderie, avec une montagne de moules-frites. Pete, viens, on t’a gardé une chaise. Massie, toi, tu fais la vaisselle.
en: Pete Hegseth deserves an A plus, plus, plus for his defence against that Massie, a sourpuss, a grump, a total loser.
Up north, the best reward isn’t a grade: it’s a seat at the braderie table, with a mountain of mussels and fries. Pete, come on, we kept you a chair. Massie, you do the dishes.
notes: The Braderie de Lille, every September, is a giant flea market where restaurants pile up the empty mussel shells outside, each one competing for the biggest heap.

texas.hook: A plus, plus, plus! *In Texas we hand out a belt buckle. Size of a dinner plate.*
texas.short: In Texas we don’t give A’s. We give rodeo belt buckles. Pete gets one the size of a dinner plate. *Massie gets a participation ribbon.*
text: Pete Hegseth gets an A plus, plus, plus for his defense against that disgruntled, angry fella Thomas Massie. A total loser, folks, believe me.
In Texas we don’t hand out A’s. We hand out belt buckles, and the bigger the buckle, the better the cowboy. Pete gets one the size of a dinner plate. Massie gets a participation ribbon.
en: He gives his Secretary of War top marks and calls the congressman who wants to impeach him a total loser.
In Texas, rodeo champions win large belt buckles instead of medals; the congressman gets only a ribbon “for taking part”.

boston.hook: A plus, plus, plus! *Harvard doesn’t even give an A plus.*
boston.short: Across the river at Harvard, the top grade is an A. No plus. *Pete just got three pluses Harvard won’t even give.*
text: Pete Hegseth gets an A plus, plus, plus for his defense against Massie, a real sore loser, an angry guy.

Now, across the river at Harvard, there’s no A plus at all. The top grade is an A, and they act like it’s a Nobel. So Pete’s got three pluses Harvard won’t even give. That’s Boston for you: we out-grade Harvard.
en: He gives his Secretary of War top marks and dismisses the congressman who wants to impeach him as a sore loser.
At Harvard, just across the Charles River in Cambridge, the highest grade is an A, with no A plus: so three pluses beat Harvard.

yorkshire.hook: A plus, plus, plus! *Round here we’d say he’s done all right.*
yorkshire.short: Round here the highest praise is “he’s done all right”. Anything more and folk wonder what you’re after. *Pete: you’ve done all right.*
text: Pete Hegseth gets an A plus, plus, plus for his defence against that Massie, a moaner, a mardy one and a total loser.
Mind you, round here the highest praise is “he’s done all right”. Anything more and folk wonder what you’re after. So, Pete: you’ve done all right. Don’t let it go to your head.
en: He gives his Secretary of War top marks and calls the congressman a sulky (“mardy”) loser.
But in Yorkshire, praise is famously understated: “he’s done all right” is about as high as it goes.

british-diplomat.hook: A plus, plus, plus! *We would have written “satisfactory”.*
british-diplomat.short: In British school reports, the usual words are “satisfactory” and “could do better”. *The latter applies, sooner or later, to almost everyone.*
british-diplomat.shortEn: He likes his Secretary. *In capital letters.*
text: His Majesty’s Government notes the President’s assessment of the Secretary of War’s performance.
British school reports traditionally prefer more measured terms, such as “satisfactory” or “could do better”. We have always found the latter to apply, sooner or later, to almost everyone.
en: He likes him a lot. In capital letters.

text: France follows the debates of the American Congress with respect, and takes note of the President’s high opinion of his Secretary of War.

In French schools, an old saying holds that twenty out of twenty is for God, nineteen for the teacher and eighteen for the best pupil. We would therefore suggest, in friendship, a little restraint in the grading.
fr: La France suit avec respect les débats du Congrès américain et prend note de la haute opinion du Président sur son secrétaire à la Guerre.

À l’école française, un vieil adage veut que vingt sur vingt soit pour Dieu, dix-neuf pour le professeur et dix-huit pour le meilleur élève. Nous suggérons donc, en toute amitié, un peu de retenue dans la notation.

text: The Federal Council takes note of the President’s assessment.
The Federal Council does not grade its members. It meets every week, takes its decisions together, and none of its members has ever received a plus, let alone three.
fr: Le Conseil fédéral prend acte de l’appréciation du Président.
Le Conseil fédéral ne note pas ses membres. Il se réunit chaque semaine, décide collégialement, et aucun de ses membres n’a jamais reçu un plus, encore moins trois.
notes: The seven federal councillors meet weekly and take their decisions as a college: no member is singled out.
